portal-ground.note: What an aperture holds before its key frame has decoded.

haze-blue.note: Painted nebula field on the band's own 27 degree axis, alpha 0.08.

name.purpose: The hero h1. Visually hidden once the stars carry the name, but never removed from the document.

name-ar.purpose: Cairo Variable, tracking reset to 0, leading opened to 1.28.

title.purpose: Every non-hero beat's h2. Nothing sits above it.

title-ar.purpose: Same clamp, Cairo Variable, no tracking, 1.28 leading.

body.purpose: At most one per beat, capped at 52ch. Dropped below 620px of frame height except the hero's.

action.purpose: A real destination with an inline SVG arrow. 44px minimum.

action-ar.purpose: 14 becomes 15.5 — a link is a word a reader must hit as well as read.

role.purpose: The hero's second line only. Uppercase dropped and stepped to 14.5px in Arabic.

star-caption.purpose: A repository's name on its own star. Full ink, uppercase, tracked.

star-caption-plain.purpose: A tool's name. One step down because twelve share one ladder; not a control.

seek.purpose: The chapter navigation. Labels, not buttons.

shadows.name: aperture-inner-fall
shadows.purpose: The only shadow on the cinema. The picture falls into the black at the rim instead of stopping at it, so the stars on the rim read as the edge.

shadows.name: archive-ambient
shadows.purpose: Inherited by the archive below the seam. Long, soft, pulled back by a large negative spread.

shadows.name: copy-scrim
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow: the edgeless field the copy sits on. Mirrored to 66% under RTL; lightened to 0.56 on the two centred beats.

shadows.name: frame-vignette
shadows.purpose: Painted grade over the canvas, with SVG fractal grain at 0.028 above it so the haze cannot band.

motion.name: morph-window
motion.purpose: The four-point beat: 47% assembly, 28% hold, 25% release. 791 / 471 / 421 px at 1440x900; floors 700 / 450 / 400.

motion.name: hero-window
motion.purpose: The hero opens already assembled; scrolling is what releases it.

motion.name: assembly-ease
motion.purpose: Fast out of the field, then a long settle onto the seat.

motion.name: release-ease
motion.purpose: It lets go slowly, then goes. Both ends have zero velocity, so no boundary reads as a cut.

motion.name: copy-arrival
motion.purpose: Copy arrives on activation by opacity and a 4px rise. Never scrubbed by scroll.

motion.name: chapter-dissolve
motion.purpose: The hidden chapter's visibility waits for the fade; inert is toggled on the same frame the renderer switches.

motion.name: hint-decay
motion.purpose: The scroll hint is gone by 3% of the runway — the first flick of a wheel.

motion.name: runway
motion.purpose: 31,500px at 1440x900 across nineteen beats. The cap held; 40 was allowed and not needed.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion:reduce — all transitions off; renderer holds drift, twinkle and every morph at pose
motion.purpose: The same composition with nothing moving in it, read through window.__mmNativeMatchMedia because the site patches matchMedia.

components.name: Action Link
components.description: A real destination on a beat. Never a second call-to-action group.
components.html: Enter the world

components.name: Star Caption (repository)
components.description: A repository's name hanging off its own projected star, with the drawn leader that keeps it attached. The anchor is a zero-by-zero point; only the chip moves.

components.name: Star Caption (tool)
components.description: A tool's name. Not a control — none of those repositories are public — so it owes no 44px target, but it keeps the full ink.

components.name: Portal Plate
components.description: A world's key frame seen THROUGH the aperture the stars opened. Sized to the rim, clipped to the ellipse, covered by the image, held at opacity 0 until the browser says it is decoded.

components.name: Portal Plate (still document)
components.description: The same key frame in the base layer: a plain picture in flow with the hairline rim it keeps in the cinema, and its intrinsic size on the element so no space shifts when the bytes land.

components.name: Seek Control
components.description: Chapter navigation for a film a keyboard has to be able to watch. A label, not a button: the border only appears when a pointer or a keyboard asks for it.
components.html: <button type="button" class="ds-seek"><svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" width="15" height="15" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 4 6 10l6 6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6"/></svg>Previous</button>

components.name: Seek Exit
components.description: The one accent-coloured control in the nav: the way out of the runway and into the archive.

components.name: Skip Link
components.description: Clipped and transparent until focused, then a control hanging off the top edge whose target is past the entire 36-viewport runway. A long runway without a way past it is a keyboard trap.
components.html: Skip the cinematic to the work

components.name: Beat Copy Block
components.description: One beat's words: the heading, at most one line, and the links — on an edgeless radial field rather than in a box. No element sits above the heading.
components.html:
Twelve tools that do the repeating.

Skills I wrote so the repeating half of the work runs itself.

narrative.overview:
This world governs the flagship portfolio's landing route and the archive that follows it on the same black. Its whole material is one particle starfield: nineteen beats in which the same stars leave the field, stand for a moment as a name, an aperture, a figure or an asterism, and are released back. There is no second population and no second illustration layer — the point cloud that is the sky is also the drawing.

The ground is pure black and there is exactly one accent. Everything readable is HTML over the canvas; nothing legible is ever drawn into the canvas. Depth is carried by three scaled shells of stars with fixed world positions, by a faint band on its own 27 degree tilt with a painted haze that agrees with it, and by grain and a vignette — never by a card, a panel or a border box.

The scoping is a load-bearing design decision, not an implementation detail. The tokens are declared on `.showroom:has(.signal)` and never on `:root`, so the cinema and the archive below it — which are siblings — both resolve them, while the site's six-theme system, the header, the top-layer dialog and every other route are untouched. The one exception is a paint rule on `body:has(.signal)`, because the body owns the page ground and is not a descendant of `.showroom`.
keyCharacteristics: Pure black ground, one accent (#8AB4FF), one ink and one secondary ink. Measured on the rendered page at 18.86:1 title, 9.76:1 body line, 18.86:1 actions and captions.

One canvas, one renderer, one scroll number. Every frame is a pure function of progress u, so reverse scroll, a restored position, a deep link and Home/End all land on the frame forward scroll produces.
The still HTML document is the base layer, not a fallback: no JS, no WebGL context and reduced motion all land on a complete, readable list of work.
A beat is 47% assembly, 28% hold, 25% release — the reading is paid for in scroll distance, not in a dwell timer.
Type is one family per language, light and small, over a soft field with no edge.

rules.name: The Colour Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Colour arrives from a real product capture — a world's key frame inside its aperture, a screenshot in the archive. Every authored surface on this route is black, ink or the one accent.

rules.name: The Nearest Ancestor Rule
rules.body: These tokens are declared on .showroom:has(.signal) and never on :root. A token on :root is the whole document and would follow the visitor into the header, the top-layer dialog and the next route; a token on .signal is invisible to the archive, which is its sibling, and an unresolvable var() computes to the guaranteed-invalid value and takes the whole declaration with it.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: One hue, one meaning: a live path the visitor can take. It never reports a status, a result or a quality.

rules.name: The Caption Is Read, Not Decoded Rule
rules.body: A name on a star is a caption: 13-13.5px, uppercase, tracked 0.11-0.13em, in the page's full ink. The leader carries the connection so the caption does not have to shout; the hairline is dimmer than the caption it serves.

rules.name: The Arabic Step Rule
rules.body: Arabic is not Latin at a smaller size. Every slot runs 1-2px larger with looser leading and no tracking: body 16/1.62 to 17.5/1.85, action 14 to 15.5, role 13 to 14.5, seek 12 to 13.5. These are steps on the existing clamps, so the responsive curve is shifted, not replaced.

rules.name: The Latin Exception Rule
rules.body: A star caption stays at the Latin size and keeps its tracking in both routes, because it is a repository or skill name marked dir=ltr. The exception needs !important because the site's global RTL rule has it.

rules.name: The Still Document Is The Base Layer Rule
rules.body: The composition the server ships is complete and worth reading on its own. The cinema is added on top of it and never supplies it.

rules.name: The One Source Of Truth Rule
rules.body: One canvas, one renderer, one scroll number. Nothing in the scene reads a clock, a random source or a previous frame, so every entry point evaluates to the same state.

rules.name: The Reading Is Paid In Pixels Rule
rules.body: A hold is measured in scroll distance against a floor, not in a fraction that looks reasonable. 202px of hold is a title, a line and a link arriving and leaving inside two notches of a wheel.

rules.name: The Scrim Has No Edge Rule
rules.body: Copy sits on a soft field, never on a box. A scrim that terminates makes the rectangle the loudest shape on screen.

rules.name: The Rim Is The Only Line Rule
rules.body: The aperture's edge is made of stars and an inner vignette. A drawn hairline circle would be a line painted over the one figure that must not have a line drawn on it.

dos: Do declare route tokens on the nearest common ancestor of everything that reads them (.showroom:has(.signal)), never on :root, and paint the body ground with a literal because the body sits above the declaring element.
Do ship the still document as the base layer: nineteen beats in document order with their real pictures, which is where no-JS, no-WebGL, a lost context and reduced motion all land.
Do gate the cinema on a live context alone, and give reduced motion the same composition held still rather than a switched-off one.
Do make every frame a pure function of one scroll number, so reverse scroll, a restored position and a deep link agree.
Do pay for reading in scroll distance: 0.47 assembly / 0.28 hold / 0.25 release, checked against floors of 700 / 450 / 400 px on the window that actually ships.
Do size a portal plate to the rim and clip it to the ellipse, and derive the rim's share of the figure's box rather than typing the ratio twice.
Do hold a picture's opacity at exactly 0 until img.decode() resolves.
Do anchor a label to a projected point and let the chip hang off it; de-collide by sliding the chip down a drawn leader, never by moving the anchor.
Do set a star caption at 13-13.5px, uppercase, tracked, in full ink, with a leader dimmer than the caption.
Do step every Arabic slot up 1-2px with looser leading and no tracking, and restate the tracking for Latin dir=ltr captions with !important, because the site's global RTL rule has it.
Do make a chapter's copy arrive on activation by opacity and a 4px rise, not scrubbed by scroll — scrubbed text parks at whatever fraction the visitor stopped at.
Do keep the composition alive on a short frame by tightening the setting, not by shortening the chapter.
donts: Don't use hue to carry a status, a result or a quality. One accent, one meaning: a live path.
Don't draw anything readable into the canvas. Type is HTML over the field.
Don't put a card, a panel or a bordered pill over the field. A control's border appears on hover or focus and not before.
Don't give a scrim a visible edge, and don't let it cover the one star a beat is about.
Don't draw a hairline over an aperture; its rim is stars and an inner vignette.
Don't hide an inactive chapter with opacity alone — visibility:hidden plus inert, so it leaves the tab order, the accessibility tree and find-in-page together.
Don't use a logical property for a position the renderer already computed from the camera's projection; that arithmetic is physical and mirroring it twice puts the element off the Arabic screen.
Don't add a second type family to this route. One family per language, inherited from the page.
Don't introduce glass, blur panels, a hard offset shadow, a system display face, or a glyph icon font; icons are inline SVG.
Don't put a kicker, eyebrow or tracked label above a heading. The tracked uppercase caption form is native to this world on a star, in a seek control and on the role line — not above a title.

Don't extend these rules past this route. The cinematic Worlds under public/worlds/, the project story routes, the work pages and the shared Contact.astro keep their own art direction and the site's six-theme system is untouched.
notCanonized: The route ships an eyebrow above every heading. .signal__kicker (11px, 500, .24em, uppercase, secondary ink) renders above the title on all nineteen beats in the still document, fed by a per-act kicker in chapters.ts COPY. The cinema hides it and the stylesheet's own comment states the ban, so it is live precisely on the layer this system calls the base layer. Recorded as a defect the build carries; no kicker token or component is defined.
.cf-kicker is hidden, not removed: the inherited Contact.astro markup still contains its eyebrow element and other routes that mount that component still show it.
Mobile Lighthouse performance is 59 on the simulated slow-4G phone (LCP 4.7s, TBT 810ms), against a measured worst p95 frame interval of 8.4ms under a 4x CPU throttle.
valid-source-maps fails in every Lighthouse run: the build ships no source maps.
